phrases.latin: Ibi jentāculum sūmpsērunt: pānem tostum cum būtȳrō et melle, sūcum aurantiōrum, pater caffeae pōcillum, avia theae.
phrases.english: There they had breakfast: toast with butter and honey, orange juice, a little cup of coffee for Dad, tea for Grandma.
phrases.source: Libellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

phrases.latin: id pater, tranquillus, nihil algēns, pōculum theae tenēns, ex altō vidēbat
phrases.english: Dad, calm, not at all cold, holding a cup of tea, saw it from above
phrases.source: Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 73.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
